academicJudgment.strongestObjection: Biology is a multiscale field with substantial plant and comparative animal science and practical formation; the UCR offer leans toward human biomedicine and ecology. A generic cells-plus-environment label, mechanical24courses or a105EC/180EC fraction would not establish comparability. Chair preparation may determine substantive later specialization and cannot simply be called administrative.
academicJudgment.decision: The fixed105EC common object is independently specified and substantial: actual cells/genetics/evolution, organismal physiology/biodiversity/ecology, experimental and quantitative methods. UCR offers sustained subject teaching across these scales, including microbial and molecular laboratory investigation, evolutionary/population mechanisms, actual biodiversity microscopy/identification, human structure-function, comparative neurobiology and ecological modelling. The strengthened broad programme adds actual chemical/physical mechanisms and environmental biogeochemical laboratory/models rather than more health/context courses. This is a meaningful broader response to the common academic object, not a degree replica. Plant physiology/reproduction, full comparative vertebrate and invertebrate/algal/fungal formation, philosophy of biology and specialist chemistry/physics/methods remain real gaps. The narrower molecular-health alternative is justified by three uniquely owned direct generators and actual topic/method allocation, without claiming full common breadth.
academicJudgment.scope: No RO3/thesis chair eligibility inferred from course prefixes, old manual, current chair lists or module assumed knowledge. Unknown chair requirements can reverse full-degree conclusions; all75EC outside105common, including known30open, are excluded in full. The fixed compulsory common object does not depend on a particular chair, background3EC or RO2 choice. The genuine 180 framework is not relabelled a completed pathway.

readerValues.programmeDescription: Study life from cells and genes through organisms, evolution and ecosystems. Wageningen Biology combines biological theory with chemistry, physics, quantitative methods, laboratory and field research.
readerValues.comparisonExplanation: This qualified comparison assesses Wageningen Biology’s confirmed 105 EC common curriculum. The two UCR programmes offer broader study of biological mechanisms from cells and genes to physiology, evolution and ecosystems, with distinct general and molecular-health emphases. They do not reproduce the full plant and animal specialisms, organismal field and laboratory formation, or all chemical, physical and quantitative methods. Background-choice study, specialisation, thesis preparation and final research are excluded.

curriculum.routeLabel: Common programme with restricted specialisation choices
curriculum.limitation: All 180 EC are retained as a supported credit framework, including 30 EC genuine open study without selected contents. Only the 105 EC common curriculum is assessed. The other 75 EC—3 background choice, 18 specialisation, 24 thesis and 30 open—are excluded. The two RO3 courses preparing for a supervising thesis chair remain unconfirmed; this is not a certified complete pathway.

componentNotes.y1-bioorganic: Introduces biomolecular structure, reactivity, stereochemistry, reaction mechanisms and molecular interactions through lectures, exercises and practical work.
componentNotes.y1-ecology1: Introduces ecological theories and principles through research and applications in nature management, agriculture, fisheries and environmental policy.
componentNotes.y1-ecology2: Complements Ecology I with data-generating field, greenhouse or laboratory investigations, a literature-based project proposal, reports and a presentation.
componentNotes.y1-cell: Studies plant, animal and bacterial cells, organelles, cellular organisation, differentiation and communication, with practical investigation and group discussion.
componentNotes.y1-analysis: Develops differentiation, integration and simple first-order differential equations for scientific applications.
componentNotes.y1-chem: Studies molecular interactions, energy exchange, thermodynamics, chemical equilibria, buffers and reaction kinetics in living systems.
componentNotes.y1-genetics: Develops inheritance, chromosome mapping, gene expression, genomics, gene manipulation, population genetics and complex traits.
componentNotes.y1-evolution: Studies evolutionary mechanisms within populations and species, selection, speciation, the history of life and comparative methods.
componentNotes.y1-zoology: Studies vertebrate structure and function, development and evolutionary adaptations through comparative anatomy and laboratory investigation.
componentNotes.y1-plants: Connects plant cells, tissues and whole-plant structure to development, photosynthesis, transport, growth regulation and interactions with microorganisms.
componentNotes.y1-biodiversity: Practises identification of Dutch plants and animals, diagnostic keys, field observations and biodiversity comparisons across habitats.
componentNotes.y1-linear: Applies vectors, matrices, linear systems, eigenvalues, iteration, projection and regression, including numerical software.
componentNotes.y1-stat2: Develops confidence intervals, tests of means, simple linear regression and correlation, checking model assumptions and good statistical practice.
componentNotes.y2-physics: Applies optics, mechanics, fluid flow, diffusion, heat and other physical principles to biological phenomena.
componentNotes.y2-reproduction: Studies plant reproductive strategies, flowering, fertilisation, embryogenesis, seeds and fruits, with practical investigation of structure and development.
componentNotes.y2-physiology: Connects mammalian organ systems, morphology, physiological regulation and environmental adaptation through practical work and a case study.
componentNotes.y2-modelling: Uses mathematical and computational models to turn biological hypotheses into predictions that can be investigated and tested.
componentNotes.y2-microbio: Studies the genetic, physiological, morphological and ecological diversity of microorganisms, supported by practical investigation.
componentNotes.y2-ethics: Examines how biology explains phenomena and informs social, animal, environmental and biotechnology ethics.
componentNotes.y2-development: Studies molecular mechanisms of plant and animal development, including differential gene expression, stem cells, communication and pattern formation.
componentNotes.y2-behaviour: Uses Tinbergen’s four questions to study animal behaviour, with practical data collection and analysis, study design and scientific writing.
componentNotes.y2-diversityskills: Nine-credit study of invertebrates, algae and fungi combines organismal laboratory work and a field course; its two teaching periods must be completed in order. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety and the zero-credit Biology Skills Portfolio remain separate requirements. The portfolio includes annual reflection and an oral test during the thesis.
componentNotes.y3-advancedstats: Six-credit compulsory study of regression, analysis of variance, categorical data, non-parametric tests and statistical designs, using R. The thesis module’s Ecological Methods alternative does not remove this programme requirement.
componentNotes.y1-mathchoice: Example for entry with VWO Mathematics A: functions, equations, differentiation and integration in Mathematics Applied: Introduction. Students with VWO Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.y2-specialisation: Illustrative restricted option for a cellular, plant or animal direction: laboratory and computational investigation of DNA, RNA and proteins, including cloning, PCR, protein analysis and enzyme kinetics. Other directions use Molecular and Evolutionary Ecology. Final specialisation and thesis preparation remain unverified. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: Required 24-credit laboratory, field or data-science/modelling research generating new data, with a plan, scientific article, presentations and defence. Before starting, complete at least 102 prescribed credits including all first-year credits and pass two RO3 courses preparing for the supervising chair. Their current allocation remains unverified. Registration at least one month before starting is mandatory; discuss a project at least four months beforehand. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.y3-ro3: Choose at least 12 credits from the prescribed RO3 list and pass two RO3 courses preparing for the supervising thesis chair. Some listed courses carry three credits, so the credit minimum and two-course condition must both be met. This reserved block is not a verified combination. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common curriculum.
componentNotes.y3-choice: Thirty credits remain open for a minor, individual minor or elective courses. This component is outside the assessed 105 EC common curriculum.
